rationale: One wrong errno constant explains every failure. socket01 asserts a 9-case table over socket(2): 3 successful creations (PF_UNIX dgram, UDP, TCP), EAFNOSUPPORT on an invalid domain, EINVAL on an invalid type, and EPROTONOSUPPORT on four domain/type/protocol mismatches (SOCK_RAW as non-root, UDP-proto stream, TCP-proto dgram, ICMP-proto stream). Reading kernel/src/syscall/socket.rs, the machinery for the whole table already exists and only the errno is wrong: every 'unsupported protocol' arm returns Errno::EAFNOSUPPORT, and grep confirms EPROTONOSUPPORT appears nowhere in kernel/src/net/ nor in socket.rs/socketpair.rs at all. The AF_INET SOCK_STREAM arm rejects protocol 17 and 1 with EAFNOSUPPORT (line ~50), the AF_INET SOCK_DGRAM arm rejects protocol 6 the same way (line ~60), and SOCK_RAW on AF_INET falls through to the outer catch-all which also says EAFNOSUPPORT. So the four EPROTONOSUPPORT cases each get EAFNOSUPPORT instead. The other five cases already pass: CSocketAddrFamily::try_from and SockType::try_from supply the EAFNOSUPPORT-on-invalid-domain and EINVAL-on-invalid-type cases, and the three valid sockets are all constructible today. The fix is a narrow errno correction plus distinguishing 'family unsupported' from 'family fine, protocol wrong' in the outer catch-all, in one 100-line function -- no new subsystem, no data-structure change, and no network device needed since socket() only allocates an fd. Measured, not assumed: this run's probe boot on base e8f2b9ca6 fails socket01 in 0.001s as a clean assert failure, and the pinned LTP 20260529 host binary passes it (cached host record, still valid since the version is unchanged). This also corrects an assumption two earlier rounds acted on: run-iIbwju and run-f6fYXT both rejected the whole socket cluster as 'broken rather than merely failing', but socket01 and socketpair01 had never actually been probed, and both fail cleanly and instantly. Ground no earlier round covered: all six committed runs are fsync03, dup02, clock_getres01, epoll_ctl02, timerfd_gettime01 (ltp) and readv_test (gvisor); none touched socket(2), and the net/socket tree is untouched by any of them. Preferred over the other clean failures probed this round. Rejected socketpair01, the closest rival and the same defect class, because it is strictly broader: beyond the shared EPROTONOSUPPORT gap it also needs EOPNOTSUPP for UDP/TCP socketpairs and two EFAULT cases for bad sv pointers, so it is three defects rather than one -- and fixing socket01 first is the natural order. Rejected epoll_ctl04 and epoll_ctl05 (both fail cleanly, both need the ep_loop_check nesting-depth and cycle detection that grep shows is entirely absent from kernel/src/events/epoll/) because run-qMdgxS already deliberately steered around epoll cycle detection to avoid overlapping run-rVlQYu's just-committed epoll_ctl02 fix, and re-picking it would repeat that collision. Rejected epoll_wait02 as a timing-jitter test (tst_timer_test sampling, inherently flaky under emulation; it took 8.3s). Rejected fcntl27 and fcntl23 as file-lease work (F_SETLEASE/F_GETLEASE is a whole feature), fcntl17 as a 576-line record-locking test that took 10s, and fcntl12 as F_SETOWN/signal-ownership plumbing. Rejected chdir01, creat08, creat09, open02 and open10 as permission- and mode-semantics clusters rather than one check.
notes: Pool entry is all.txt:1593, exactly '# socket01'. Default configuration: the entry is in all.txt and in neither blocked/ext2.txt nor blocked/exfat.txt, so no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR override and run_vars is empty. Host baseline was not re-run this round: socket01 already had a cached host=pass at LTP 20260529, which is the pinned version in test/initramfs/nix/conformance/ltp.nix, and host records do not go stale when Asterinas changes. Cache handling: the 379 host records remain valid, but of the pre-existing probe records 87 are from commit 68bdd4a99, which is NOT an ancestor of this run's base e8f2b9ca6 (parallel branches), so per cache.md those are weak hints only and their fails were re-probed rather than trusted. Ground chosen deliberately: the 50 candidates already measured host=pass/probe=fail at e8f2b9ca6 had all been weighed and rejected or taken by rounds 1-4, so this round probed the 168 candidates that had a valid host=pass but had never been probed in Asterinas at all, plus 14 set-B entries whose only probe was on the parallel branch. Appended 37 records to select.cache: 29 probe (8 pass, 14 fail, 7 broken recorded as fail with "state":"broken") and 8 stale-entry. Those 8 already pass in Asterinas at e8f2b9ca6 while still commented out in all.txt and are the readiest work for later rounds -- open06, open08, preadv02, pwritev02, read03, readv02, rmdir02, write04. Five results were skips (getcwd04, lseek11, lstat03, timer_delete01, unlink09) and are not cached, since skip maps to none of the four valid result values; a later round should not read their absence as unmeasured-and-promising. Probing constraint later phases should know: the runner redirects kirk's stdout to a log file it only cats after the run completes, so a hang loses every per-test result. mprotect04 hung and, with the script's LTP_TIMEOUT_MUL=5 against kirk's 300s default, would have burned 25 minutes and taken the whole batch's results with it; two boots were lost that way before this phase temporarily changed the redirect to a tee and set LTP_TIMEOUT_MUL=1 to take its measurements. That edit has been reverted -- git status in the worktree shows only the expected untracked .osdk/. mprotect04 is therefore unmeasured, not passing, and mprotect01 came back broken. For diagnose: the four failing cases are tdat[3] SOCK_RAW, tdat[5] UDP stream, tdat[6] TCP dgram and tdat[8] ICMP stream; note Protocol::try_from accepts 1/6/17 as valid enum variants, so the failure is purely the errno chosen by the match arms, not a rejected conversion. Also note socketpair.rs:51 carries the identical EAFNOSUPPORT catch-all, so a shared helper may be the cleaner fix, but socketpair01 stays blocked this round.
